title: Agent Memory Is a Surface for Endogenous Authorization Laundering

source.authors: Tommaso Cerruti, Mika Okamoto, Ansel Kaplan Erol

takeaways.claim: Incremental memory writers can generate or preserve false authorization without an external attacker.
takeaways.caveat: Evaluated on synthetic histories and calibrated executors.

takeaways.claim: Typed incremental memory produced 27.7 percent unauthorized actions on average versus 0.8 percent for typed one-shot in the reported aggregate.
takeaways.caveat: Specific models, domains, tasks and memory construction; not a production rate.

takeaways.claim: In matched memory repair tests, false-authority propagation was 99.0 percent, falling to 1 of 390 with oracle-exact memory.
takeaways.caveat: Ground-truth oracle is unavailable to ordinary deployed agents.

takeaways.claim: A deterministic current-authorization source should be separated from persistent agent context.
takeaways.caveat: This is an engineering inference, not a production-tested paper result.

limitations: Synthetic task histories and domain-proxy tools
